ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: It is known that the point $(-3,-1)$ and the point $(4,-6)$ are on two sides of the line $3 x-2 y-a=0$, then the range of values of $a$ is ( )
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: According to the problem statement, define the directed expression of the line as F(x,y)=3x-2y-a. The two points are P=(-3,-1) and Q=(4,-6). Substituting gives F(P)=3(-3)-2(-1)-a=-9+2-a=-7-a; F(Q)=3(4)-2(-6)-a=12+12-a=24-a. Because the two points are on opposite sides of the line 3x-2y-a=0, the corresponding directed values have opposite signs, that is, (-7-a)(24-a)<0. Solving this inequality, the critical values are a=-7 and a=24, and checking gives that when -7<a<24, the product is less than 0. Therefore the range of values of a is (-7,24).
